description: issue #681 (slice I2): `spec/interaction-events.md:131` — "`ol-type` if the prompt cannot be displayed as learner text", which the profile`s error table (`:350`) classes as "an argument has the wrong type". The accepted prompts are the scalars `word`, `number`, and `boolean`, whose printed form IS the characters shown; a `list` (here), `dict`, or `record` renders as a bracketed container view and a `turtle` as the opaque identity tag `turtle #<id>` (`spec/turtles-and-sprites.md:13`) — a rendering of a structure, not a question authored for a person to read and answer. IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED BOUNDARY, recorded deliberately: `spec/execution-model.md:552-574` gives every value a printed form, so the spec does not itself say where "has a printed form" ends and "learner text" begins. This fixture takes the narrower reading because the wider one would leave the normative `ol-type` clause unreachable for every input, and an unimplementable normative error is worse than a boundary drawn in the open. A maintainer ruling that widens it should relax this fixture. The span points at the offending prompt argument, not the whole call. The diagnostic carries the `{ operation, expected, actual }` identity shape the profile`s other `ol-type` builders use (`when`/`on_key`), with `expected: "text"` naming the spec`s own phrase. The prompt is validated BEFORE the read, so the answer queue is untouched and no `primitive` event is emitted — a rejected prompt must not silently consume the next answer and leave every later read off by one.

diagnostics.message: input needs a prompt it can show as text, but got a list.
